$Comment: The off-ladder BOSS tier. Roll.Weight 0 keeps it out of the normal weighted roll; it is granted exclusively through Families.ForceGroups, which claims every role in the Mmoscaling_Bosses NPCGroup tagset. Add roles to that tagset (or role-name globs to Families.ForceRoles here) to hand them this tier. Force bypasses the weight, the difficulty band, the rarity spawn chance, and the allow/deny gate, but it is a FLOOR: a normal roll that lands on a stronger tier still wins, and 'stronger' is decided by DifficultyMultiplier, so keep this one the highest on the ladder. DifficultyMultiplier 3.0 folds a boss at three times the spot's difficulty, so at the top of the shipped scale (MaxCap 200, read at 600) it comes to about 32 times an unscaled mob's toughness and about 266 times its hit. The plain mob standing beside it at 200 is itself scaled, to about 11.5 times and 58 times, so against that plain mob the boss is about 2.8 times as tough and hits about 4.6 times as hard (the damage curve bends upward, so a multiplier on difficulty buys more damage than toughness). Both figures sit just under the two safety rails of 34.4 and 270: the rails never flatten the shipped boss, and they are what stops the numbers running away if you raise this multiplier, stack a variant on the tier, or lift MaxCap. A per-world Pool.Rarities deny for 'boss' still suppresses it in that world. Its Loot borrows the legendary drop table and, at Multipliers.Loot 3.0, rolls it three times per kill; give a boss its own table or its own extra rolls here when you want a distinct prize. DecorateName false keeps the boss's own name in death messages and the kill feed (an Ember Dragon, not a Boss Ember Dragon); the mob inspector still tags it Boss. Set it true to print the tier there too.
Name: Boss
